new_statements.quote: Stems end in a vowel and generally receive the accent on this vowel, that is, the accent indicates the morphological right edge of the stem. Nevertheless, the accent may sometimes appear on the first syllable of the stem: compare the examples in (1a-3a) where the first syllable is accented with (1b-3b) where the accent falls on the second syllable. [...] (1) a. wéra-ni 'go out' b. wera-ni 'cry' (2) a. kára-ni 'fly' b. kara-ni 'write' (3) a. píri-ni 'approach' b. piri-ni 'sing' [fn. 3:] In these examples, we may observe that the final vowel is elided when it is not stressed. The accent appears on the first or second syllable of the stem. [p. 7:] it is easy to distinguish the verbal root from the derivational element since the latter is not accented and is suffixed to the former.

Nevertheless, the accent may sometimes appear on the first syllable of the stem: compare the examples in (1a-3a) where the first syllable is accented with (1b-3b) where the accent falls on the second syllable. I indicate the accent only when it appears on the first syllable.' followed by (1) wéra-ni 'go out' / wera-ni 'cry', (2) kára-ni 'fly' /…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog lists Purepecha with an empty rule and no existing stress statement; this work supplies the placement (stem-edge accent, lexically contrastive first- vs second-syllable stems, suffixes unaccented), so it adds where the catalog is blank rather than contradicting anything.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent sits on the stem (root), never on a suffix: as a rule it falls on the stem-final vowel (the right edge of the stem, i.e. the second syllable of a disyllabic stem), but a lexically fixed subset of stems accent their first syllable instead, giving minimal pairs (wéra-ni 'go out' vs wera-ni 'cry'). Since suffixes are unaccented, surface accent is on the first or second syllable of the word. Unstressed final vowels are elided.
new_statements.exceptions: First-syllable stems (wéra-ni, kára-ni, píri-ni) contrast lexically with second-syllable stems (wera-ni, kara-ni, piri-ni); the author marks accent orthographically only when it is on the first syllable. Derivational suffixes are never accented.
new_statements.identity_note: Chamoreau's examples and morphological tables are from the Jarácuaro variety (Lake Pátzcuaro, eastern area; she says so explicitly for Tables 4-5 and the enclitic system). The accent statement is presented as general Purepecha and no dialectal variation in accent placement is mentioned, though she notes dialect variation elsewhere in morphology.

tone_statements.quote: El purépecha tiene una ventana acentual de las dos primeras sílabas del radical, su acento es demarcativo y nunca recae en los morfemas. ... el patrón rítmico que forma es trocaico, fuerte(*)-débil(.) en la mayoría de los casos. ... Este ritmo fue atestiguado en dos comunidades, en la sierra por Agustín Diego (2016) y en el lago por Montellano Moreno (2021). En este último trabajo se propuso que la lengua es entonativa ... [respuesta del autor a los dictámenes:] Se especifica que es una lengua entonativa con lo que denoto que no es tonal
tone_statements.translation: Purepecha has an accentual window of the first two syllables of the root; its accent is demarcative and never falls on the (suffixal) morphemes. ... the rhythmic pattern it forms is trochaic, strong-weak, in most cases. ... This rhythm was attested in two communities, in the Sierra by Agustín Diego (2016) and at the lake by Montellano Moreno (2021). In the latter work it was proposed that the language is intonational ... [author's response to reviewers:] It is specified that it is an intonational language, by which I mean that it is not tonal
tone_statements.locator: §2 'Descripción de la lengua' journal galley (article pp. 65-97; page numbers not), plus the appended author's response to reviewers
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: No lexical tone (language characterised as intonational, not tonal). Word accent lexically on sigma1 or sigma2 of the root (left-edge two-syllable window), never on suffixes; trochaic secondary rhythm; F0 peaks are postlexical pitch accents (H*, L+H*, etc.) aligned to stressed syllables, with L boundary tones; accentual phrase = H* at left edge + L at right edge.
